uncited: It differs from [Smooth SDF Composition](2685-smooth-sdf-composition.md) by aggregating multiple distinct primitives into a single scene-level distance field rather than composing a single smooth blend of shapes.
- For each sphere $i$, evaluate the sphere SDF: $d_{sphere} = \| p - c_i \| - r_i$.
- For each cuboid $j$, evaluate the cuboid SDF.
This involves transforming $p$ into the cuboid's local space (if rotated), computing the distance to the box, and returning the result.
- Precision issues may arise if primitives are extremely close or overlapping, though the min operation handles overlaps correctly for unions.
This is the dual of the union operation used in the main scene evaluation.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N)$, where $N$ is the total number of primitives in the scene.
Each primitive is evaluated exactly once.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N)$ to store the primitive data structures.
Not suitable for very large scenes without spatial acceleration structures (which are not part of this basic evaluation method).
The method originates from ray marching techniques using Signed Distance Functions.
